# `.trit` package byte layout v1.0

All offsets are from the start of the file. Multibyte header integers are unsigned little-endian.

## Header (64 bytes)

| Offset | Size | Field | Required value / meaning |
| ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| 0 | 8 | Magic | `TRITIUM\0` |
| 8 | 2 | Major version | `1` |
| 10 | 2 | Minor version | `0` |
| 12 | 4 | Required features | `0`; unknown bits reject the package |
| 16 | 8 | Manifest offset | Absolute file offset |
| 24 | 8 | Manifest length | Exact byte length |
| 32 | 8 | Directory offset | Absolute file offset |
| 40 | 8 | Directory length | Exact byte length |
| 48 | 16 | Reserved | Must be zero |

## Blob store

Blobs are deduplicated by BLAKE3 of their exact stored bytes. Each unique payload begins at an offset aligned to 256 bytes; padding bytes are zero. Blobs are placed in ascending digest order. The manifest follows the final blob and the directory follows the manifest.

Directory entries are sorted by blob digest, then semantic kind. The canonical-CBOR directory is `[version, entries]`; each entry is `[digest, kind, auxiliary, offset, length]`, where digest is a 32-byte byte string and offset/length are unsigned integers. Kind tags are `0` = additive tensor (`null` auxiliary), `1` = dense tensor (dtype text auxiliary; accepted values: `ternary`, `i4`, `i8`, `u8`, `f8e4m3`, `f8e5m2`, `f4e2m1`, `f16`, `bf16`, `f32`), and `2` = asset (nonempty name text auxiliary). Directory version is `1`.

The manifest and directory use deterministic CBOR. Floating-point manifest values are rejected. Manifest size is limited to 268435456 bytes, directory size to 268435456 bytes, and writer input and directory entries are each limited to 1000000 records.

## Footer (72 bytes)

The footer begins immediately after the directory and is located at end-of-file. It contains `TRITEND\0` at relative offset 0, the BLAKE3 digest of the exact manifest bytes at relative offset 8, then the BLAKE3 digest of the exact directory bytes at relative offset 40.

The reader rejects truncated ranges, nonzero reserved/padding bytes, unknown required features, unsupported versions, noncanonical metadata, overlapping/out-of-range blobs, and digest mismatches.
